idiom_name: expression body plus Unit, and also/apply returning the receiver
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes the value part of the declaration: a single-expression function returns its expression, a function with a block body must declare its return type except when that type is Unit, and Unit never has to be returned explicitly. The standard library supplies both realizations of the pattern - also and apply perform a side step and return the context object, while let, run and with return the lambda result - so the call site states which of the two it wants instead of leaving it to convention. Keep block bodies short, declare the return type explicitly on public functions, and use apply for object configuration where the receiver itself is what the caller continues with.
pitfalls: also and apply return the receiver, not the lambda result: using x.also { it.compute() } where the computed value was wanted silently yields x.

A block body that ends with a computation but no return statement is a Unit function - Kotlin will not let the value escape, so the interesting value must be returned explicitly or the function rewritten as a single expression.
A lambda whose last expression has a value can still be passed where a () -> Unit function type is expected, and the value is discarded there.
